In this regard it would be appropriate to reproduce provisions of Section 13 (1) and (2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 which read as follows:
13. Report of public analyst.

- (1) sh The public analyst shall deliver, in such e form as may be prescribed, a report to the ad Local (Health) Authority of the result of Pr the analysis of any article of food submitted to him for analysis.

a (2) On receipt of the report of the result of hy the analysis under sub-section (1) to the ad effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority M shall, after the institution of prosecution of against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the rt person, if any, whose name, address and ou other particulars have been disclosed C under Section 14A, forward, in such h manner as may be prescribed, a copy of ig the report of the result of the analysis to H such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may take an application to the Court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory.
17.
From perusal of the above provision, the word used is adulterated and not mis-branded.
The charge against the petitioner is for mis-branding and not for adulteration.
Therefore, this objection raised by the petitioners does not hold good.
